scope: Historical-scholarship content gaps after published revision 1.164; review and research priorities only. No canonical acceptance, graph mutation, publication or OpenAlex work.

limits: The frozen release is a bounded repository sample of History PhDs; frequencies represent consultation in recovered bibliography/notes, not quality, agreement or influence.

All-authorship people.csv counts, first-author unions and work counts are different measures. All first-author and work counts here were recomputed from frozen citations/dissertations/works; variant work keys remain separate.
No top-500 lead count is adopted without release comparison. No count is summed across title variants, countries or author aliases.

prior_work_review: Reviewed decisions.csv from canonical-work-gaps-2026-10-24. These recommendations do not repeat resolved 148-row person-work chronology/edition findings. Roediger explicitly treated as development, not a missing existing work.
main_finding: The clearest historical-scholarship omission is a connected body of US social/political/cultural scholarship: Reconstruction, New Deal labour/consumption, immigration/racialization, masculinity and grassroots conservatism. Global colonial legal history is another substantive gap. Several Canadian/environmental figures lack standalone biographies but their ideas already have detailed content.
